preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(line.split()[0]) <= 2000 for line in stdin.splitlines()[:2])
preconditions.description: The first two lines contain integers n and m, where 1 ≤ n, m ≤ 2000, representing the maze dimensions.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(line.split()[0]) <= n and 1 <= int(line.split()[1]) <= m for line in stdin.splitlines()[2:4])
preconditions.description: The third and fourth lines contain integers r, c (1 ≤ r ≤ n, 1 ≤ c ≤ m), representing the starting cell coordinates.

preconditions.expression: all(0 <= int(line.split()[0]) <= 10**9 and 0 <= int(line.split()[1]) <= 10**9 for line in stdin.splitlines()[4:5])
preconditions.description: The fifth line contains integers x, y (0 ≤ x, y ≤ 10^9), representing the maximum allowed left and right moves.

preconditions.expression: len(stdin.splitlines()) == n + 5 and all(len(line) == m for line in stdin.splitlines()[5:5+n])
preconditions.description: The next n lines describe the maze, each line has exactly m characters ('.' or '*').
The starting cell (r, c) is guaranteed to be free ('.').

postconditions.description: The output is a single integer representing the number of reachable cells from the starting cell, including the starting cell itself.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= i <= n and 1 <= j <= m and (stdin.splitlines()[i-1][j-1] == '.' or (i == r and j == c)) for i, j in reachable_cells)
postconditions.description: A cell (i, j) is counted as reachable if it is either the starting cell or a free cell ('.') and there exists a path from (r, c) to (i, j) with at most x left moves and y right moves, without moving beyond maze boundaries or through obstacles.
The output integer exactly matches the count of reachable cells as defined in Q2.
